int_name: E HUNTING PARK AVE & K ST

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps. However, the environment is primarily designed for vehicle throughput with wide lanes and minimal physical separation or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A dark SUV is parked very close to the intersection on the left, potentially blocking the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: Visible cracking and wear on the asphalt surface near the crossing area could present a trip hazard or affect vehicle braking.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past parked cars before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard transverse markings to high-visibility continental or ladder style markings to increase driver awareness.

result.summary: The environment features a wide multi-lane roadway with a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While the crossing is signalized, the lack of a median refuge and the long crossing distance create significant exposure for pedestrians in a high-speed design context.

hazards.name: Excessive crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a wide multi-lane roadway without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to traffic.

hazards.name: High-speed roadway geometry
hazards.description: The wide, open street design lacks physical traffic calming measures, which can encourage vehicle speeds higher than appropriate for an urban environment.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island at the crosswalk to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian access with sidewalks and traffic signals but lacks high-visibility crosswalk markings and dedicated pedestrian signals. Parked vehicles near the corners create potential sightline obstructions between drivers and people attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalks
hazards.description: The absence of painted crosswalks at a signalized intersection fails to designate a clear path for pedestrians and reduces driver awareness.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners may block the view of pedestrians for turning motorists.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and prevent parking too close to the intersection.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street that is highly hostile to pedestrians due to a complete lack of dedicated walking infrastructure. There are no visible sidewalks or marked crossings, forcing pedestrians to share the roadway with vehicles on a wide, straight street that likely facilitates higher speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: No paved walkways exist, forcing pedestrians to walk in the travel lane or on unpaved shoulders.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the scene.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing Points
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks leaves pedestrians unprotected when attempting to cross the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line can hide pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Parked cars on the left and right sides of the street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide a safe, separated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Implement marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns at intersections to designate safe crossing locations.
